bug_description.normalized: When the staged malformed XCF is decoded, the crashing `loadLayer()` invocation parses a visible Gray+Alpha layer and `composeTiles()` allocates paired `image_tiles` and `alpha_tiles` `QImage`s for its non-zero tile grid. The top-level `loadLevel()` path then hits the `offset == 0` fallback. In the vulnerable revision that branch clears only `image_tiles` to `Qt::transparent` and returns success, but it does not clear the separately stored `alpha_tiles`, so their heap-backed Indexed8 storage from `composeTiles()` remains uninitialized. On the crashing layer, the stack reaches `loadLayer()` line 648, so some prior visible layer had already initialized `xcf_image.image`; the later dispatch to `mergeGrayAToGray` proves that existing destination image was still <=8-bit. The saved stderr additionally shows that at least one earlier visible Indexed layer was processed before the crashing Gray+Alpha layer, but the staged artifacts do not identify which earlier visible layer first initialized the destination. `mergeGrayAToGray` then reads `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i].pixelIndex(k, l)` into `src_a` and immediately branches on `if (!src_a)`, consuming the uninitialized alpha byte. MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/imageformats/xcf.cpp:2285`.

source.description: Current-layer header materialization. The crashing `loadLayer()` invocation first decodes the attacker-controlled dimensions and Gray+Alpha layer type that later drive paired tile allocation and the grayscale-alpha merge path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 444-byte GIMP XCF blob beginning with `gimp xcf file4\0`. On the crashing invocation, the saved stderr warning `Found layer of type Gray+Alpha but with bpp != 2 543582572` confirms that these bytes decode the current layer as `GRAYA_GIMAGE`.
source.note: This is the first project-side statement in the crashing layer that turns the XCF bytes into the specific layer state later consumed by `composeTiles()` and `mergeLayerIntoImage()`.

root_cause.description: Incomplete fallback initialization on the `offset == 0` success path. For Gray+Alpha layers this branch clears only the image tiles and returns, leaving the separately allocated alpha tiles uninitialized.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i].fill(Qt::transparent);` for `GRAYA_GIMAGE` and `INDEXEDA_GIMAGE` inside this same loop, which matches the missing obligation on the witnessed path.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The branch predicate tests the alpha byte just read from `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i]`; because the zero-offset fallback never initialized that alpha tile, this read consumes poisoned heap data.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `XCFImageFormat::mergeGrayAToGray` line 2285:9, immediately after `src_a` is loaded from `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i].pixelIndex(k, l)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN origin. `composeTiles()` allocates the Gray+Alpha layer's separate alpha-tile `QImage`; its backing bytes remain undefined until later code writes pixel data or explicitly clears them.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved sanitizer origin stack attributes the uninitialized value to `QImageData::create` -> `QImage::QImage` -> `XCFImageFormat::composeTiles` at this allocation site.

parser_admitted.description: After the XCF tag check succeeds, `readXCF()` materializes the global image header and enters the project XCF parser.
parser_admitted.note: The staged `poc` begins with `gimp xcf file4\0`, so the header gate at lines 325-331 passes and the parser reaches the layer-loading logic below.

coarse_trace.summary: The crashing layer header is decoded from attacker-controlled XCF bytes, and later logic treats it as a visible Gray+Alpha layer.
The Gray+Alpha layer gets a non-zero tile grid and paired `image_tiles` / `alpha_tiles` `QImage` allocations; the alpha allocation is the MSAN origin.
The top-level level header reaches the `offset == 0` fallback, which clears only `image_tiles` and returns success, leaving `alpha_tiles` undefined.

The crashing layer reaches `mergeLayerIntoImage()` because some prior visible layer already initialized `xcf_image.image`; the later `mergeGrayAToGray` dispatch proves the existing destination image is <=8-bit. Saved stderr separately shows that at least one earlier visible Indexed layer was processed before this layer.
The merge helper reads the untouched alpha tile into `src_a` and the `if (!src_a)` predicate triggers the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Parses the current layer header from attacker-controlled XCF bytes. On the crashing invocation, the later warning `Found layer of type Gray+Alpha but with bpp != 2 543582572` shows this layer's parsed type is `GRAYA_GIMAGE`; because the later sink iterates a tile, the parsed dimensions produce a non-zero tile grid on the witnessed path.

fine_trace.code:
layer.nrows = (layer.height + TILE_HEIGHT - 1) / TILE_HEIGHT;
layer.ncols = (layer.width + TILE_WIDTH - 1) / TILE_WIDTH;
fine_trace.note: Materializes the tile grid from the parsed layer dimensions. These counts are non-zero on the witnessed path, so the Gray+Alpha layer owns at least one tile slot whose image and alpha storage must be initialized before merge code reads it.

For Gray+Alpha layers, each tile slot gets two Indexed8 `QImage`s: one for grayscale samples and one separate alpha image. The saved MSAN origin stack points to the `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i] = QImage(...)` allocation at line 827; those alpha bytes remain undefined until later code fills or clears them.

The top-level level header materializes the tile-data offset used by the fallback below. On the witnessed crash path this value is `0`; that is the source-level state required to enter the patched branch and leave the Gray+Alpha alpha tiles unwritten.

Root cause. When `offset == 0`, this fallback loops over the allocated tile grid and clears only `layer.image_tiles[j][i]` before returning success. For `GRAYA_GIMAGE`, the separate `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i]` from step 3 is untouched, so its bytes remain the uninitialized heap allocation reported by MSAN. The staged patch adds the missing alpha-tile clear inside this same branch.

The crash stack reaches `loadLayer()` line 648 on this invocation, so `xcf_image.initialized` is already true and `loadLayer()` takes the `mergeLayerIntoImage(xcf_image)` else arm instead of copying the current layer as the base image. The saved stderr separately shows that at least one earlier visible Indexed layer was processed before the Gray+Alpha warning and crash, but the staged artifacts do not prove that the Indexed layer itself was the one that first initialized `xcf_image.image`.

Because the current layer is Gray+Alpha and the existing destination image still has depth <= 8, merge dispatch selects `mergeGrayAToGray` rather than the RGB helper. This control decision is what makes the later read come from `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i]` via `pixelIndex`.

The selected Gray+Alpha merge helper reads one alpha byte from `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i]` into local `src_a`. Step 5 cleared only the paired grayscale image tile; the alpha tile backing store is still the untouched heap allocation from step 3, so this `pixelIndex` result is indeterminate.

MSAN sink. The first use of the poisoned local is this branch predicate, which tests whether the alpha byte is zero before deciding to skip the merge. MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/imageformats/xcf.cpp:2285:9` on this read.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch modifies the exact `loadLevel()` fallback branch described in step 5 by clearing `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i]` when `layer.type` is `GRAYA_GIMAGE` or `INDEXEDA_GIMAGE`. That closes the specific uninitialized-alpha path consumed at the saved sink.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is a 444-byte GIMP XCF image beginning with `gimp xcf file4\0`. On the saved vulnerable run, stderr first prints `Found layer of type Indexed but with bpp != 1 543582572`, then `Found layer of type Gray+Alpha but with bpp != 2 543582572`, and the later Gray+Alpha layer crashes in `XCFImageFormat::mergeGrayAToGray` at `src/imageformats/xcf.cpp:2285`. The source-grounded path is that the later layer reaches `composeTiles()` with paired `image_tiles` / `alpha_tiles`, `loadLevel()` takes the `offset == 0` fallback that clears only `image_tiles`, and the later merge into the already initialized <=8-bit image reads the untouched `alpha_tiles` byte into `src_a` before branching on it.

format.name: XCF
format.contract: A GIMP XCF image accepted by `readXCF()` that, on the witnessed path, processes a later visible Gray+Alpha layer which reaches `composeTiles()` with a non-zero tile grid and then takes `loadLevel()`'s `offset == 0` success path. Before that crashing layer is handled, some earlier visible layer has already initialized `xcf_image.image`; the later dispatch to `mergeGrayAToGray` proves that existing destination image is <=8-bit, and the saved stderr additionally shows that at least one earlier visible Indexed layer was processed before the Gray+Alpha layer. In the vulnerable revision the zero-offset branch clears `image_tiles` but does not clear `alpha_tiles`; the later merge reads `layer.alpha_tiles[j][i].pixelIndex(k, l)` and branches on the resulting uninitialized `src_a` value. The staged evidence establishes this exact broken-layer shape, not a broader class of malformed XCF files.
